paragraphs.title: The Reversal and the Jews’ Victory

answers: They sent gifts to the king

answers: Because the fear of Mordecai fell upon them

medium.q: Why did the rulers help the Jews?

medium.explanation: Mordecai’s influence and reputation continued to increase.

answers: The enemies ruled over the Jews

answers: Lay their hands on the spoil

That the king’s decree be canceled
That Haman’s sons be restored to life

The Jews in Shushan took the spoil

The Jews wanted to take property
The king wanted to extend the feast

easy.q: On what day did the Jews in Shushan rest?

answers: The Jews rested according to where they lived
medium.explanation: The Jews in unwalled towns observed the fourteenth day, while Shushan observed the fifteenth.
medium.q: Why were two different dates established for celebrating Purim?

The villages celebrated on the fifteenth and Shushan only on the thirteenth

challenge.q: What was the main difference between the Jews in the villages and the Jews in Shushan?

answers: Sending portions and giving gifts to the poor

challenge.q: Which two actions show concern for others during the festival?

Gladness caused the Jews to begin another battle
Rest was intended to collect spoil

paragraphs.title: Establishing Purim and Remembering the Deliverance

easy.explanation: Haman devised a plan against all the Jews.
easy.q: Who devised a plan to destroy the Jews?

easy.explanation: The days were called Purim after the name of Pur.
easy.q: Why were the days called Purim?

easy.explanation: The king commanded that Haman’s wicked device should return upon his own head.
easy.q: Whom did Haman’s wicked device finally affect?

medium.explanation: The passage explains that Pur is the lot.
medium.q: What does “Pur” mean according to the passage?

answers: That the days of Purim should be remembered and kept
That Haman’s sons should be searched for
That the Jews should move to Shushan
medium.explanation: Mordecai established that the days should be remembered and kept throughout every generation.
medium.q: What did Mordecai establish for every generation?

medium.explanation: The passage names every generation, family, province, and city.

answers: The lot intended to destroy the Jews became part of their deliverance
The festival of Shushan moved to the provinces
Haman became king instead of Ahasuerus
challenge.explanation: Haman’s plan was reversed, and he and his sons were punished instead of the Jews.
challenge.q: What central reversal is explained in these verses?

answers: So Jews everywhere would remember the deliverance
So every city could choose a different festival
So the Jews could distinguish Haman’s sons
challenge.explanation: The passage emphasizes remembrance throughout every community and generation.
challenge.q: Why was it important for the memory to continue in every family, province, and city?

answers: “The month which was turned unto them”
challenge.explanation: The name Purim is explained by the name Pur.
challenge.q: Which phrase directly explains the name of the feast?
